To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
explicit image quality rules enable compliance to safety standards in computer vision.
explicit rules for low-level quality detection of images in computer vision applications are feasible and that they facilitate complying with safety standards.
the proposed image quality rules enable detection of image quality problems that can be used to improve the safety of computer vision systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality and usability in computer vision by developing rules that enable low level detection of quality problems.
the question of how to detect image quality problems in computer vision and the implications of such detection for safety.
developing and demonstrating explicit rules for image quality detection that enable the development of compliant safety-critical computer vision systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed rules enable low-level detection and analysis of image quality problems, which can be used to support compliance with standards in computer vision.
the proposed rules can be applied to detect quality problems in an image, and that the proposed method is a promising step towards compliance with standards in computer vision.
the presented approach enables compliance to safety standards and thus facilitates real-world applications of computer vision in safety-critical systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be used as a first step in the safety analysis of a computer vision system.
we have developed explicit image quality detection rules and a method to use them to improve safety in image processing.
the presented rules can be used as a basis for a functional safety analysis of image processing in a computer vision system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
image quality problems can be identified at a very low-level of image processing, and the results can be used to trigger more advanced and computationally expensive image processing algorithms.
the rules are applicable to a broad range of image processing applications and that they can be used as part of a safety case to demonstrate compliance with safety standards.
the rules can be used for detecting image quality problems that can be used for compliance with standards, such as IEC 61508 and ISO 13849.
